prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: Building on c011 (timing-driven weighting + decay<=0.5, score +0.453), the remaining lever is the *upper bound* on net weights: with `max_net_weight` at infinity a few critical nets dominate and starve the many moderately-critical nets that drive TNS. Clamping `max_net_weight` to a moderate finite value (e.g. 8) keeps the weighting responsive but spreads gain across more nets, which should reduce TNS further without hurting WNS, and it is a pure, generalizable parameter with no legality risk (unlike the aggressive decay=0.25 that crashed c012).
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.619 robust(mean-std)=+0.190 min_case=+0.184 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.212 dWNS=+21.2% dTNS=+21.5% overflow~105
  bp-ng45: score=+0.184 dWNS=+11.0% dTNS=+23.3% overflow~114
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.223 dWNS=+9.3% dTNS=+31.0% overflow~104
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Hypothesis held: clamping `max_net_weight` to 8 improved all three cases, with TNS gains (+21.5%, +23.3%, +31.0%) exceeding WNS gains (+21.2%, +11.0%, +9.3%), consistent with spreading weight across moderately-critical nets rather than letting a few dominate. Robust score +0.190 and min_case +0.184 confirm no case regressed. Next step: sweep `max_net_weight` (e.g. 4, 6, 8, 12) to locate the TNS-optimal clamp, since 8 may not be the sweet spot.
